evidence.note: differs only by a trailing slash

output.fix: Make the redirect_uri sent in the authorize and token requests identical to a registered one. Either drop the trailing slash in the client or register "https://app.example.com/callback/" as well. The comparison is an exact string match. For local development, register each origin you use as its own redirect URI, for example http://localhost:3000/callback and http://127.0.0.1:3000/callback. The authorization server treats localhost and 127.0.0.1 as different hosts. Keep PKCE S256 as it is.

alternatives.why_not: The code_verifier matches the S256 code_challenge, so PKCE passes.
The public client with the authorization_code grant and S256 passes the client config check.

questions: The captured request uses https://app.example.com/callback/, not a localhost or 127.0.0.1 URI. Which redirect_uri does the localhost:3000 versus 127.0.0.1:3000 setup actually send, and is each one registered?
